newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso closes weaker on dlr short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso closes weaker on dlr short-covering.

text.p: The Mexican peso closed weaker on Monday after dealers covered short dollar positions ahead of the end of the month, on what dealers said was a slow session due to the absence of U.S. players.
"Some opened short and began to buy dollars to square their books, as a precaution with the close of the month coming up," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate both closed 3.5 centavos weaker, at 7.9130/7.9160 and 7.9100/9130 per dollar, respectively.
Same-day peso dealing was suspended because U.S. financial markers were closed for Memorial Day.
Dealers said the peso also softened on forecasts primary Cetes rates would fall again at Tuesday's primary central bank auction.
"They covered (dollar) shorts before the month ends, and then there's the auction, at which Cetes rates could fall a little," another trader said.
Dealers differed over the predictions for Tuesday's session, although few expected the peso to trade at less than 7.90 per dollar.

"Foreigners could decide it is worth selling dollars at current levels when they return tomorrow, or they may exert pressure if they too need to cover (dollar) shorts," one trader said. (( --Alexis Quiones, Mexico City newsroom +525
